description:
FILED s536d (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08) while taking #4625's bar.  PRE-EXISTING: this is the "ran 1 of 1008, rc 1" face of the IO-Compress 105oneshot family that #4625 attributed to the `my $name` cell.  The cell was #3493 (s536d fixes it: a full run now reads pass=971 fail=37, no "NO!!!!"); the FLIP is this.

MEASURED (s536d tree, gen v2-12400, `tools/run-dist-t.pl --rows ~/.cpan/build/IO-Compress-2.214-0 t/105oneshot-deflate.t` five times in a row, logs scratch/s536d/io5-N.log in the s536d worktree): run 1 HEAP, run 2 HEAP, run 3 COMPLETE (pass=971 fail=37), run 4 HEAP, run 5 COMPLETE (pass=971 fail=37, the same rows as run 3).  Not cold-vs-warm: run 4 follows a complete run 3.

THE DIE: `Heap exhausted during garbage collection: 0 bytes available, 64 requested.` / `fatal error ... Heap exhausted, game over.` with the backtrace SB-REGALLOC::GROW-SC / PACK-TN / PACK <- SB-C::%COMPILE-COMPONENT <- COMPILE-IN-LEXENV <- %SIMPLE-EVAL <- EVAL-TLF <- LOAD-AS-SOURCE <- LOAD <- PCL::%P-LOAD-TEXT-STREAM <- PCL::%P-LOAD-MODULE-UNCACHED <- %P-LOAD-UNIT <- P-LOAD-MODULE-CACHED <- %P-REQUIRE-GUARD <- %P-REQUIRE-RUN.  `t/compress/oneshot.pl` is one `sub run { ... }` of ~1,300 source lines; its emission is ~338 KB (`./pl2cl --module < oneshot.pl`), and the whole sub is ONE top-level form, compiled by `compile` inside the program's own 1 GB image every run.
QUESTIONS (the discriminating measurements, not taken): (1) why is a `require "oneshot.pl"` loaded UNCACHED (a .pl under the dist's t/?  the #2702 first-run path?) -- a cached fasl would compile once, in the builder; (2) the peak heap of `(compile nil '(lambda () <run body>))` alone in a fresh image (is it ~1 GB, or does the program's own heap state decide?).
Rows: the four 105oneshot *PLAN* rows of baselines/cpan-board14-fails.tsv (re-keyed by s536d to this task).


=== MEASURED (s539a, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-13) -- no code changed; the levers are below ===
THE TWO DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENTS:
(1) WHY UNCACHED: a board run sets `*pcl-skip-cache*` (tools/run-dist-t.pl line ~202: `(setf pcl::*pcl-skip-cache* t)`), so EVERY module of a board file -- the dist's .pm files and `require "oneshot.pl"` alike -- loads through %p-load-module-uncached: transpiled, then its text compiled by SBCL in the program's own image.  It is not specific to a `.pl` nor to #2702's first-run path.  In an ordinary run (cache on) the file is a :local module (under t/), so the transpile is cached but the TEXT is still compiled every run -- the module-cache policy s540d is changing (#4986: local modules compiled once).
(2) THE PEAK HEAP of that compile: the file's emission is 335,601 bytes, ONE top-level form of 301,245 (the `sub run`; the next largest 26,913).  A driver = 105oneshot-deflate.t up to and including `require "oneshot.pl"` (no run()), the board's way (skip-cache, cwd = the dist), base core 24988e35, scratch/s539a/legs/m7-heap.sh + m7-heap.log in the s539a worktree, 3 runs per cell (load 5-9: times are noisy, rc / RSS are not):
  policy    heap MB   result      max RSS          load+compile time
  default    768      3/3 HEAP EXHAUSTED  770 MB    63-74 s
  default   1024      3/3 complete  766 / 766 / 967 MB  73-81 s
  default   1536      3/3 complete  1,159 / 1,159 / 837 MB  68-78 s
  cheap*    1024      3/3 complete  700-702 MB      74-79 s
  interpret 1024      3/3 complete  105 MB          46-58 s (no compile; run() not measured)
  * (proclaim '(optimize (compilation-speed 3) (speed 0) (space 1) (debug 0) (safety 1))) before the load.
So the giant form's compile peaks at 0.77-0.97 GB in a 1 GB heap: the s536d flip (2 of 5 died in SB-REGALLOC) is GC timing near the ceiling, not a leak.
THE LEVERS: (a) compile the required file ONCE into the module cache (a builder with its own heap) = the module-cache POLICY, s540d's #4986 -- not built here (the brief: do not touch it); with the board's skip-cache flag the board would also need its runner to stop skipping the cache for dist modules.  (b) a cheaper policy for an oversized form: -9..-28 % peak RSS at 1 GB (700 MB vs 766-967), compile time unchanged -- shipping it needs the four files 5 of 5 + the bench inside 3 %, not taken (budget); `:interpret` for that one form removes the compile (105 MB) but the 1,008 rows would run interpreted (unmeasured, likely much slower).  (c) the emitter splitting a giant sub at statement level: design only -- the sub body's let-bound lexicals would have to be shared across the chunk lambdas (boxes already are; raw slots would need to be boxed or passed), and `return` / `next` / `last` / `goto` crossing a chunk boundary need the non-local exits the emitter already has for closures; cost: a new pass over the CLForm of one sub, plus the verdict machinery's assumptions about one lambda per sub.
THE USER's NUMBER: PCL_DYNAMIC_SPACE_MB=1536 completes the require 3 of 3 here (peak 0.84-1.16 GB).  Not changed (the heap default is the USER's).
subject: NONDETERMINISTIC: IO-Compress t/105oneshot-*.t die "Heap exhausted, game over" in SB-REGALLOC while COMPILING oneshot.pl's one giant `sub run` -- the required .pl is loaded UNCACHED from text every run (%p-load-module-uncached), and whether the 1 GB heap suffices flips run to run (the *PLAN* `ran 1` state; #4625's flip)
